subject: Special warranty carveout & pricing corridor — request for executive sign-off
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@biometrix.com>, procurement@biometrix.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Special warranty carveout & pricing corridor — request for executive sign-off

Hi Elena / Biometrix team,

Thank you again for the productive workshop last week — really appreciate the pragmatic approach from your product and procurement teams. We’ve prepared a clean SOW and tracked redlines for the commercial and legal terms (attached). Two items came up where we need senior authorization before we can finalize:

1) Warranty language: Biometrix is asking us to remove our standard warranty carveouts for third-party model outputs and add a 24-month express warranty for service levels and accuracy. Legal has pushed back; Biometrix cites regulatory exposure for certain healthcare models.

2) Pricing corridor / first-year discount: Commercial is proposing a stepped discount schedule tied to committed spend. To hit competitive economics for a pilot to production path, they’re asking for a 35% discount in year 1 if Biometrix commits to a 12-month minimum usage and a $350k committed spend.

Requested approvals (what I need from Redwood leadership):
- One-time exception to reduce our liability cap to $2,000,000 (from standard $5,000,000) for this account, contingent on a certificate of insurance naming Redwood and a carveout linking IP indemnity to willful misconduct.
- Acceptance of the limited warranty carveout in the attached redline where warranty is restricted to "conforming to the SOW and not covering model output downstream usage".
- Approval for the proposed pricing corridor: 35% discount in year 1, 25% in year 2, with the discount conditioned on the signed SOW and committed spend milestones.

Attachments: Biometrix_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW draft), Biometrix_term_redline.docx (tracked changes).

If legal needs to see an alternative compromise, please advise. We’re on a tight timeline — Biometrix wants a final contract by end of next week to align with their board meeting.

Next steps I propose: legal to provide redline guidance, commercial (Rishi) to confirm revenue and commit thresholds, then exec sign-off if acceptable.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if useful to walk through the trade-offs.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Enterprise

Chloe —

Thanks for the summary and the redlines. High-level legal position: we can be flexible commercially, but the warranty and indemnity asks as drafted create outsized exposure. Specific concerns:

- Full removal of warranty carveouts for third-party model outputs is not acceptable. We can consider a narrow, time-limited warranty tied to specific performance SLAs in the SOW (e.g., availability and inference latency), but we must exclude downstream regulatory liability and harms arising from customer model usage.

- Liability cap: dropping to $1M is outside our risk tolerance. $2M is a possible business decision, but we need commercial mitigation (higher committed spend, larger upfront payment, or insurance certificate). If you want $2M, we should require Biometrix to carry technology errors & omissions insurance naming Redwood and provide evidence prior to signing.

- Indemnity: we cannot accept broad IP indemnities if we’re being asked to carve out warranties. Maintain IP indemnity for third-party claims but limit scope to claims directly arising from Redwood-delivered code.

I’ve annotated the redline with suggested language (see Biometrix_term_redline.docx). Please capture the commercial trade-offs (ARR potential, strategic value, churn risk) so leadership can weigh the request. If leadership prefers to keep $5M cap, we can propose alternative commercial concessions.

I’m happy to escalate for a senior exception if you confirm commercial justification.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Laura / Chloe / team —

Thanks — quick context from commercial side to inform the escalation:

Business rationale:
- Biometrix is a strategic play: they run clinical decision support models and, if successful, plan enterprise-wide deployment across 4 lines of business. We’re modeling ~ $3.8–4.5M ARR inside 18 months with typical expansion.
- They’re prioritizing Redwood for performance/latency and observability; this deal would be a strong healthcare reference.
- Short-term economics are tight because they want a pilot-first approach and need a low-barrier pricing corridor to justify the internal pilot budget.

Proposed commercial compromise (my recommendation):
- Liability cap: approve a $2,000,000 cap (not $1M) conditioned on Biometrix providing a COI (E&O insurance) naming Redwood with $5M coverage and an addendum that ties IP indemnity to Redwood-originated code only.
- Warranty: accept a limited warranty that covers service availability and conformance to SOW performance metrics for 12 months post-go-live. Explicitly exclude downstream decisions and model outputs beyond the SOW scope.
- Pricing corridor: we can approve 35% off list in year 1 but limit the effective discount to a minimum committed spend of $350k for year 1 and an upfront 30% of committed year-1 fees. Year 2 discount steps down to 25% only if growth milestones are met.

If leadership approves these bounds, legal can finalize redlines and I’ll confirm paperwork with procurement. If leadership wants more protection (higher cap), I can look to soften pricing or require a larger upfront payment.

Please advise who should sign off on the risk trade-off. If Aditya or Marissa approve, we’ll send the final SOW for signature and route through DocuSign.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Team —

I’ve reviewed the notes from legal and commercial. Given the strategic upside and the reference value in healthcare, I approve a conditional exception on the following terms (final approval contingent on legal inserting the agreed language):

1) Liability cap: set at $2,000,000 total for the SOW term. Condition: Biometrix must provide an E&O certificate naming Redwood with minimum $5M coverage and list Redwood as an additional insured where appropriate.

2) Warranty: limited warranty only — 12 months post-go-live and restricted to service availability and SOW-conforming performance metrics. Explicit exclusion for downstream model decisions and regulatory harms.

3) Indemnity/IP: maintain IP indemnity for Redwood-delivered code; no indemnity expansion for third-party model outputs.

4) Pricing corridor: approve up to 30% discount in year 1 (not 35%) provided Biometrix signs the 12-month committed spend of at least $350k and pays 30% of year-1 committed fees upfront. Year 2 discount may step down to 20% upon meeting growth milestones; finance to approve exact billing structure.

Operational requirements before signature:
- Legal to finalize the redline and confirm the exact COI language.
- Finance to confirm discount mechanics and sign-off on deferred revenue treatment.
- CS to confirm rollout milestones and acceptance criteria in the SOW.

Chloe / Rishi: proceed to finalize the draft with these edits, upload the revised DocuSign package to the HubSpot deal (link below), and let me know when it’s ready to route.

Aditya Rao
